name: James A. Rice, Jr.
tagline: Top rated Personal Injury attorney in Atlanta, Georgia
education: University of Florida Levin College of Law
about: For 30 years, James A. Rice Jr. has focused on legal issues of personal injury for those in Atlanta, Georgia. At Rice McGowan & Brandt, he handles cases of premises liability, workers’ compensation, head and brain injuries, truck collisions and car accidents, as well as products liability and wrongful death. With prior experience with advocating for the defendant, he now focuses his efforts strictly on representing those who have been injured due to the negligence or poor decisions of others.

Mr. Rice is a member of the Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum and the Million Dollar Advocates Forum. Dedicated wholeheartedly to his clients and their future, he often takes cases that are referred by past clients. This highlights the confidence clients have in his ability to reach an amicable resolution for others who are suffering from an injury.

Mr. Rice graduated with honors in 1994 from the University of Florida Fredric G. Levin College of Law. After earning his Juris Doctor, he was admitted to practice in the state of Georgia in 1995. For his uncompromising ethical standards and relentless work ethic, he is peer-review rated AV Preeminent* through Martindale-Hubbell.

As he advocates for his clients and defends their right to a bright future, Mr. Rice is not afraid to turn down unacceptable offers and take a case all the way through trial if necessary. Focused on individual representation for each client and a unique strategy for every case, he is committed to going the distance to get his clients the compensation they deserve for their injuries and bring positive changes to their lives.

*AV®, AV Preeminent®, Martindale-Hubbell Distinguished and Martindale-Hubbell Notable are certification marks used under license in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies. Martindale-Hubbell® is the facilitator of a peer review rating process. Ratings reflect the anonymous opinions of members of the bar and the judiciary. Martindale-Hubbell® Peer Review Rating™ fall into two categories – legal ability and general ethical standards.
